walkthroughs.body_html:
Nucleic Acids — a core area of Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Nucleic Acids brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Nucleic Acids.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which scientist proposed 'omnis cellula e cellula' (all cells from pre-existing cells)?
options: Schleiden
Schwann
Virchow
Hooke

mcqs.q: The fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane was proposed in 1972 by:
options: Watson and Crick
Singer and Nicolson
Schleiden and Schwann
Margulis and Lovelock

mcqs.q: During an action potential, do Na+ and K+ move through the same channels?
options: Na+ and K+ swap places through the same channel at the same time.
No — voltage-gated Na+ channels open first (depolarisation, Na+ in), then voltage-gated K+ channels open (repolarisation, K+ out).
X-linked conditions affect only males because females cannot inherit X-linked alleles.
Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.

mcqs.q: What happens to an enzyme when it is denatured?
options: Its tertiary structure (3D shape) changes, particularly the active site, so it can no longer bind substrate effectively.
The enzyme has died because enzymes are alive.
The enzyme has been completely broken into amino acids.
Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.

mcqs.q: Why are X-linked recessive conditions more common in males?
options: X-linked recessive conditions affect more males because the Y chromosome makes the disease worse.
Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed — there's no second X to mask it.
Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.
X-linked conditions affect only males because females cannot inherit X-linked alleles.
